title: Johns Hopkins LSTM click detector lets a man with ALS spell 10.2 characters a minute for 90 days without retraining
summary: A chronically implanted high-density ECoG BCI with an LSTM click detector trained on under 44 minutes of data supported switch-scan spelling for 626 minutes over 90 days, all in the laboratory.
account: Candrea et al. (Communications Medicine, 22 October 2024) report a clinical-trial participant with ALS (NCT03567213) at Johns Hopkins. He had a chronically implanted high-density electrocorticographic BCI over sensorimotor cortex. High-gamma power vectors from 128 channels fed a long short-term memory layer with 25 hidden units and fully connected layers. These classified rest versus grasp every 100 ms. The click detector was trained on almost 44 minutes of data (480 trials) collected up to 21 days before use. It then ran for 90 days without retraining. The participant controlled a switch-scanning speller for a total of 626 minutes with a median spelling rate of 10.2 characters per minute. The paper states all data collection and testing were performed in the laboratory. No home use is reported. The date is the publication date.
purpose: Restore text communication for a person with ALS through a single neural click command driving a switch-scanning speller
system: Click-based electrocorticographic brain-computer interface with an LSTM click detector (NCT03567213)
model_version: LSTM (25 hidden units) with two fully connected layers, Keras/TensorFlow 2.8.0
developer: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine (Crone lab and co-authors)
segment: People with ALS and impaired speech or movement

ratings.reason: Functional text-based communication at 10.2 characters per minute in laboratory sessions totaling 626 minutes over 90 days. No home use.

ai_role.statement: The LSTM click detector is the decoding element. Its stability without retraining is the paper's main result. The source is a peer-reviewed report by the developers, with no outside corroboration and no use outside the laboratory.

metric: median spelling rate of 10.2 characters per minute

comparator.against: the Utrecht fully implanted switch-scan BCI reported by Vansteensel et al. (four contacts over hand motor cortex)
comparator.before: a spelling rate of 1.8 letters per minute with a latency of at least 1 s per click
comparator.after: a spelling rate of 10.2 CCPM and 0.68 s latency
comparator.quote: In that study a participant with ALS was implanted with four contacts over hand motor cortex and achieved a spelling rate of 1.8 letters per minute with a latency of at least 1 s per click (compared to a spelling rate of 10.2 CCPM and 0.68 s latency reported in the present work).

later.note: A search found an October 2025 medRxiv preprint on longitudinal gesture decoding from the same CortiCom trial, but medRxiv blocked both fetch methods, so no later development could be verified.
